nodes.title: Security: three certification write routes have NO per-record access check - POST /:id/verify, /:id/share and /:id/recertify, while /:id/revoke checks the issuer and /issue gates on a write role
nodes.description:
## BLUF

`POST /api/certifications/:id/verify`**,** `/:id/share` **and** `/:id/recertify` **carry no per-record access check.** They look a certification up by primary key and act on it. The only authorization on the path is the router-wide `authenticate()` plus tenant scoping, so **an authenticated caller in the same tenant** can reach a certification they are not a party to. The sibling write `POST /:id/revoke` **does** check (`certification.issuer.id !== issuer.id` -> 403), and `POST /issue` gates on a write role — so this is a gap between sibling routes in one file, not a missing convention.

Found while building the read bound for [KS-1695](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1695) (PR #1667), by enumerating every by-id lookup in the file. **Facts only; no remedy proposed.** The read gap and this are the same class on different verbs.

## Measured at develop `7e3b9362e08b` (file: `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/routes/certifications.ts`)

| route | opens | by-id lookup | `isAllowedByRoleOrScope` | `403` occurrences | per-record check |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `POST /issue` | `:180` | — | **1** (`:234`) | 5 | role/scope gate |
| `POST /:id/revoke` | `:1064` | `:1086` | 0 | **1** | **YES** — `issuer.id` mismatch -> 403 |
| `POST /:id/verify` | `:1139` | `:1150` | 0 | **0** | **NONE** |
| `POST /:id/share` | `:1209` | `:1232` | 0 | **0** | **NONE** |
| `POST /:id/recertify` | `:1310` | `:1332` | 0 | **0** | **NONE** |

**The whole file has exactly one router-level gate:** `certificationsRouter.use(authenticate())` at `:65` — authentication, no role term, no record term. `isAllowedByRoleOrScope` appears **twice in the file in total**: the import at `:48` and the single call at `:234` inside `POST /issue`.

**Instruments, and the control for each.**

* The per-route counts are a line-span census of each route's body. **Control: the counter is not stuck at zero** — the same census returns `isAllowedByRoleOrScope = 1` for `POST /issue` and `403 = 1` for `/:id/revoke`. An earlier run of this same census was discarded because a shell quoting fault made `sed` error and every count read `0` from empty input; the zeros above come from a run whose control fires.
* A body census cannot see a middleware gate, so **all four route headers were read directly.** Every middleware array holds only `express-validator` terms (`param`, `body`) — no rbac middleware on any of them.

**A claim in the file that this falsifies.** The comment above `:234` reads: *"KS-547 (KS-540 F-2): certification issuance gates like every other document-write verb — this was the one ungated write on the platform."* On the same router, three write verbs are ungated beyond authentication. Whatever was true when KS-547 shipped, "the one ungated write" does not describe this file now.

## What each route does once it is past the lookup

* `/:id/share` takes `recipients[].email` **from the caller** (validated as an email, `:1212-1217`) and creates share records for a certification the caller need not be a party to. It checks `status === 'revoked'` and nothing about who is asking.
* `/:id/recertify` mints a verification certificate against the original (`originalCert`, lookup `:1332`) and writes a `RECERTIFY` lineage event.
* `/:id/verify` reads and returns verification data; `getUserFromRequest` is not even consulted for a 401, unlike the other two.

## NOT measured — read this before acting on the table

* **None of these three routes was run.** There is no Docker on the host this was found on, so every row above is a source read at one sha, not an observed response. No status code in this ticket was returned by a server.
* **The audience is stated as "an authenticated caller in the same tenant", deliberately.** Gate BX1's measured phrase for the *read* routes — "every same-tenant user of any organisation" — is **not** carried over here, because nothing was executed against these routes and no reader role was tried. Whether a role incidentally blocks any of them is unverified.
* **Whether a share yields the sharer content they could not otherwise see is UNREAD.** `saveShare`, the share mailer, and the lineage share surface were not opened. The documents read admits a `recipientEmail`, and share delivery emails a link — either could matter, neither was followed.
* Whether `/:id/recertify`'s minted certificate is readable by, or attributed to, the caller: not traced.
* Tenant resolution uses `getReqTenantId`, which **falls back to a fixed default tenant** when `req.tenantId` is unset (`:107`, `DEFAULT_TENANT_ID`). What that means for these three routes specifically was not measured.
* **Not a duplicate, as far as a weak instrument can say.** `searchIssues` is unusable for counting here: a nonsense control term (`qqzz-control-term-no-such-thing-5417`) returned **12 hits, identical to every real term**. So candidates were read rather than counted. [KS-834](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-834) **is NOT this** — it concerns the **api-gateway's** mock verify route (`services/api-gateway/src/routes/verification.ts:556`) being mounted with no auth handler: a different file and a different route that shares the URL path. [KS-1664](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1664) is recertify's anchor-before-write ordering, not access. Nothing was found covering share or recertify access — stated as "nothing found", not "nothing exists".
